title: Inference encoding boundary
description: The inference module encodes and decodes JSON with the JSON library the project already depends on. It does not hand-roll an escaper and it does not reach for the YAML parser. Discharged by the reference-boundary checker in verification support, which scans the module source. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/inference-provider.feature.
rationale: The request body was built twice: once by a Serialize implementation the contract scenario checked, and once by a format! string with a hand-written escaper that was what actually reached the provider. Two encoders for one document drift, and these had already drifted in shape while every attestation stayed green, because the tested encoder was not the sent one. The response was decoded by serde_yaml, a crate deprecated upstream, parsing a JSON document, while serde_json was already in the dependency graph. Both are the anti-NIH rule read backwards: a maintained library was present and the project wrote its own instead. Forbidding the two references is what keeps the second encoder from growing back, since nothing about a hand-rolled escaper announces itself and the sent document has no other check that reaches it.
